title: Release Weekforge cadence and orchestra shortlist - 2026-05
content:
Release Weekforge: cadence + orchestra shortlist (compact runbook)

Purpose
- Short, actionable field guide for the week-long cadence we're trialing (Weekforge).
- Blend of a daily checklist, lightweight calendar, and the release notes draft that goes with the cutover.
- Focused on small-batch feature rollouts to Dedicated and Hosted API with observability-first gating.

Quick summary
- Window: Mon 2026-05-11 through Fri 2026-05-15 (primary ops hours 09:00-18:00 PT).
- Scope: tiered rollout of model-routing changes + two config flags (cache-ttl and batching-profile).
- Goals: validate latency SLOs, ensure no >2% error-rate regression, confirm cost delta <10% for peak paths.

Weekforge cadence (daily beat)
- Mon (Prep + Dry-run): final preflight, smoke on staging -> brief operator handoff at 16:00 PT.
- Tue (Micro-canary): 0.5% traffic to variant A, observe 3h signal window.
- Wed (Scaled small): 5% to variant A + 0.5% to B (routing experiment). 6h signal window.
- Thu (Regional widen): increase to 20% in low-risk regions (EU-west, us-west). 8h window.
- Fri (Full tilt / Holdback decision): if signals green, progress to 50% and schedule finish; otherwise unwind.

Operators and contacts (shift roster)
- Primary ops: Aisha Patel (on-call lead)
- Secondary: Marco Gonzalez (serving runtime), Emily Chen (observability), Jared Singh (release engineer)
- Pager / Slack channel: #release-weekforge (ops/alerts)

Preflight checklist (to run before Monday cutoff)
- [ ] Code and infra PRs merged and CI green (github.com/redwood-inference/*). PRs: infra/pull/782, api/pull/301.
- [ ] Staging smoke tests: latency / correctness / KV-cache warmup (3 iterations).
- [ ] Canary config bundle pinned and uploaded to S3 (s3://releases/weekforge/2026-05-11).
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards cloned and annotated for this run (links in linked_artifacts).
- [ ] Rollback plan documented and validated with SRE (runbook id: CONFLUENCE-RELEASE-1412).
- [ ] Customer-impact list reviewed; any high-risk customers notified 48h before (email template prepared).

Runbook: daily operator checklist (short)
- Affirm smoke metrics baseline (p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, token-cost).
- Start micro-canary via routing policy -> deploy variant with consistent hash seed.
- Monitor live traces for error spikes; run fast-query for recent failed requests (last 15m).
- If threshold breached (p99 > 2x baseline OR error-rate > 2%), trigger immediate throttle (roll back routing to prior variant) and call SRE.

Rollout lanes (shortlist)
1) Fastpath (low-latency experiments)
   - Target: non-critical internal clients, A/B only.
   - Steps: deploy variant, 0.5% -> 5% -> 20% if green.
   - Owners: Marco (deploy), Emily (dash scrutiny).
2) Measured (cost/perf mix)
   - Target: general public in low-traffic hours.
   - Steps: throttle-based ramp, batching-profile toggled in config for measured runs.
   - Owners: Jared (config), Aisha (decision).
3) Fallback (disaster escape)
   - Full traffic revert to baseline model routing; automated if commit-age > 15m post-threshold.
   - Owners: SRE shift (primary).

Telemetry sampling plan
- Sampling windows: continuous, but extra traces enabled for 5% of shifted traffic (trace-level = full).
- Synthetic probes: run synthetic prompt set (n=40) every 10 minutes during windows.
- Alerting: set temporary alerts for the week (p95 latency > threshold, error spike RI>2).

Comm plan (who says what)
- Internal ops update cadence: 10:00 and 16:00 PT standups (short thread in #release-weekforge).
- Customer comms: prepared short note for status page if rollback > 30m.
- Exec update: daily summary to Product & Eng-Leadership at 18:30 PT (email template in linked_artifacts).

Release notes (draft - to be cleaned and published post-finish)
- title: Model routing tuning and batching profile improvements (Weekforge May 2026).
- audience: external (developers using Redwood API) + internal.
- short blurb: "Rolling out targeted routing changes to improve small-sequence latency and recommend new default batching profile for cost reductions in low-throughput scenarios. Monitoring closely; see changelog for details."
- notable changes:
  * Introduced variant-based routing for low-latency paths (opt-in via routing.policy=weekforge).
  * New batching-profile: small-batch-eco (reduces per-token cost for short seqs).
  * Cache TTL default reduced from 120s -> 60s for routed variants.
- breaking/compat notes: no breaking API changes. Potentially different latency profile for some long requests; see caveats.
- migration: customers can opt into the variant via header X-RW-Routing: weekforge or via the Console toggle.

Known risks and unresolved items
- Risk: quantization fallback may amplify p95 latency for longer sequences when small-batch-eco is used. Need a short perf-run on long-tail prompts (JIRA-RELEASE-2891).
- Resolved? Not yet — plan a targeted long-tail perf job on Thu morning. Owner: Marco.
- Open question: do we expose batching-profile in the hosted API UI or keep as advanced config? Product to decide by Tue.

Rollback decision matrix (simple)
- Immediate rollback: any customer-facing error spike > 3% sustained over 10 minutes OR p99 > 3x baseline.
- Auto-throttle (gradual rollback): p95 degradation between 1.5x-3x baseline -> reduce variant traffic by 50% and re-evaluate.

Post-release tasks (Fri + next week)
- [ ] Collect annotated changelog entries from runtime, console, obs teams.
- [ ] Run 72h stability check; schedule follow-up perf tuning sprint if needed.
- [ ] Retrospective: 30-minute async doc (what went well / what to change) due by Wed 2026-05-20.

Retro prompts (to fill after finish)
- Did our telemetry windows capture long-tail behaviors?
- How tight were our rollback criteria — too sensitive or too lax?
- Should Weekforge be a monthly ritual or a dedicated release lane?

Notes to self / TODOs
- Prep the synthetic probe set (Emily) and attach to this doc before Monday.
- Confirm SLO thresholds with Product by Tue morning.
- Triage list for immediate post-canary follow-ups: perf_noise_detector logs, KV-cache hit-rate dips, cost-sample report.

Appendix (quick links & references)
- Runbook: CONFLUENCE-RELEASE-1412
- Canary job: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/actions/workflows/canary.yml#L12
- PRs: infra/pull/782, api/pull/301

-- end of compact Weekforge runbook --
